samples.input: According to Dr. Fuhrman, what is the maximum amount of saturated fat anyone should eat per day?
samples.target: No more than five grams of saturated fat a day.

samples.input: What is Dr. Fuhrman's advice to pregnant women about seafood?
samples.target: He advises pregnant women to completely avoid seafood products, because it is too difficult to know what pollution they contain.

samples.input: According to Dr. Fuhrman, how much extra protein per day does even a professional body builder need to build one-half pound of extra muscle per week?
samples.target: Only about an extra seven grams per day over a normal protein intake.

samples.input: In the Apple Walnut Surprise recipe from Dr. Fuhrman's Disease-Proof Your Child (serves 6), how much ground flax seed is used?
samples.target: 4 heaping tablespoons of ground flax seeds.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's vegan lentil main dish topped with a roasted-garlic cauliflower puree (made with cashews and hemp seeds), how long is the unpeeled garlic roasted?
samples.target: About 25 minutes, or until soft.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of smart supplementation, which five nutrients does he say may be below optimal levels on a plant-based diet?
samples.target: Zinc, vitamin B12, iodine, vitamin K2, and vitamin D.

samples.input: How does Dr. Fuhrman keep his vegan algae-based DHA supplement fresh from packaging through storage?
samples.target: It is packed in dark glass (not plastic) and kept under refrigeration, shipped to the warehouse in refrigerated trucks, and stored refrigerated there.

samples.input: According to Dr. Fuhrman's updated view on omega-3 status, what omega-3 index should a person be above for the ideal level?
samples.target: Above 5 or above 6.

samples.input: Dr. Fuhrman says the mortality risk of having a low omega-3 index is comparable to what smoking habit?
samples.target: Smoking two packs of cigarettes a day.

samples.input: Does Dr. Fuhrman's Gentle Care multivitamin contain iron?
samples.target: No, Gentle Care does not contain iron.

samples.input: How many different mushroom extracts are in Dr. Fuhrman's mushroom chai powder?
samples.target: 10 different mushroom extracts.

samples.input: Dr. Fuhrman offers his multivitamin in versions with and without iron; what tool does he provide to help people choose between them?
samples.target: An algorithm on his website where people enter their blood test results (ferritin levels and CBC) to get a recommendation.

samples.input: According to Dr. Fuhrman, at roughly what rate do calories from oil enter the bloodstream?
samples.target: About 100 to 120 calories a minute.

samples.input: What food combination does Dr. Fuhrman call "the witch's cauldron of cancer causation"?
samples.target: The combination of animal protein and high-glycemic carbohydrate (e.g., meat with white-flour bread, "meat and cake").

samples.input: Which common cancers does Dr. Fuhrman say synthetic folic acid promotes?
samples.target: Breast cancer, prostate cancer, and colon cancer.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's exercise demonstration, why does he have people practice side-to-side shuffle-and-stop movements?
samples.target: Because as people get older they fall sideways and break their hips, and they are not used to stopping themselves and pushing themselves back.

samples.input: According to Dr. Fuhrman's Women's Daily +D3 product information, how much vitamin B12 does he recommend taking daily, and why that amount?
samples.target: 75 mcg daily, to ensure absorption of the Daily Value of 2.4 mcg, since only a small proportion of ingested B12 is absorbed.

samples.input: How much taurine does Dr. Fuhrman's Women's Daily +D3 multivitamin supply?
samples.target: 50 mg of taurine (Men's Daily +D3 supplies a higher dose).

samples.input: Which two supplements sold by Dr. Fuhrman are exceptions to his otherwise all-vegan product line?
samples.target: Mega EPA (made with fish oil) and Designs for Health GLA-240 (which uses gelatin soft gels).

samples.input: How much calcium does Dr. Fuhrman's Women's Daily +D3 contain, and from what source?
samples.target: A conservative 200 mg dose of calcium from mineral-rich seaweed.

samples.input: What is the recommended daily dose of Dr. Fuhrman's Pixie Vites chewable multivitamin for children aged 1-3 versus 4-10?
samples.target: One chewable tablet daily for ages 1-3, and two tablets daily for ages 4-10.

samples.input: What sweetener does Dr. Fuhrman's Pixie Vites children's chewable multivitamin use instead of added sugar?
samples.target: Xylitol.

samples.input: Why do the Apple Delight overnight oats sold in Dr. Fuhrman's shop use Ceylon cinnamon rather than cassia cinnamon?
samples.target: Because cassia cinnamon contains high levels of coumarin, which can be toxic to the liver.

samples.input: How many levels of transition to a Nutritarian diet does Dr. Fuhrman's book Eat for Health provide?
samples.target: Three levels of transition.

samples.input: How much long-chain omega-3 does a 0.75 ml dose of Dr. Fuhrman's DHA+EPA Purity deliver?
samples.target: Over 250 mg of long-chain omega-3 fatty acids.

samples.input: How many organic mushroom concentrates are in Dr. Fuhrman's Immune Biotect supplement, and what else is in its blend?
samples.target: Nine organic mushroom concentrates, blended with organic berries and astragalus root.

samples.input: How many grams of sugar are in Dr. Fuhrman's G-BOMBS Chocolate Peanut Butter nutrition bar, and how is it sweetened?
samples.target: Only 8 grams of sugar, sweetened with real fruit.

samples.input: How much zinc does Dr. Fuhrman's Gentle Care multivitamin supply per serving, and in what forms?
samples.target: 7.5 mg of zinc per serving, as zinc bisglycinate and zinc picolinate.

samples.input: On Dr. Fuhrman's Eat to Live podcast episode about drinking water, what is the most liquid he says to have with a meal, and why?
samples.target: No more than half a cup, so as not to dilute digestive enzymes.

samples.input: On Dr. Fuhrman's Eat to Live podcast episode about water intake, how many cups of water a day does he say a person on the standard American diet may need?
samples.target: About nine cups of water a day.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of beverages, how much caffeine does he say naturally low-caffeine green teas contain compared with a cup of coffee?
samples.target: About 20 milligrams, compared to about 80 milligrams in a cup of coffee.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of sugar and beverages, what limit does he describe on dates used to sweeten his daily dessert?
samples.target: No more than one date per person, other than the fruit content.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of carbohydrates and flour, which breads does he say he eats, and why?
samples.target: Ezekiel bread or manna bread, because they are made from sprouted grains that are coarsely ground rather than fine flour.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of hydrogen water, why does he dissolve a hydrogen pill in water rather than use a hydrogen water machine?
samples.target: Because the hydrogen pill puts more hydrogen into the water than a hydrogen water machine does.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of sodium, how much sodium per calorie does he say natural foods like fruits, vegetables, beans, and nuts contain?
samples.target: Always less than half a milligram of sodium per calorie.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of nuts and weight loss, what is the most nuts he says overweight people should eat with each meal?
samples.target: Generally no more than half an ounce of nuts per meal.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of protein on a Nutritarian diet, roughly how much protein does he say is obtained per 1,000 calories?
samples.target: About 30 grams of protein per 1,000 calories.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of calcium supplementation, what dosing pattern does he say studies support instead of taking 1,000 mg at once?
samples.target: A low dose of food-derived calcium, about 200 milligrams with each meal.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of eating green vegetables and salads, how many times does he suggest chewing each mouthful?
samples.target: About 30 times, until it is a liquid, to maximize nutrient absorption.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what does he recommend as a baby's first food?
samples.target: Banana mashed with breast milk, or organic brown rice cereal made for babies mixed with pure water and breast milk.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, at what age does he say children may be given whole nuts, and what nut foods are fine earlier?
samples.target: Not until age two and a half (choking hazard); raw nut butters and foods made with ground raw nuts are fine after nine months.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how often does he say a new solid food should be introduced to an infant after six months?
samples.target: One new food every two days, so parents can watch for signs of allergy or sensitivity.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how long does he strongly recommend breast-feeding be continued?
samples.target: To at least eighteen months, and preferably two years or longer.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what does he recommend between twelve and eighteen months for a child who cannot be breast-fed until age two?
samples.target: A DHA-supplemented cow's milk formula.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how much DHA should a breast-feeding mother take daily, and why?
samples.target: About 200 mg of DHA daily (plus a multivitamin), to assure adequate DHA in her breast milk.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what percentage of the calcium in milk versus in bok choy does he say is absorbed?
samples.target: About 32 percent from milk versus 54 percent from bok choy.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what is the maximum amount of beta-carotene he says a children's supplement should contain?
samples.target: No more than 2,500 IU of beta-carotene, and even less is better.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what kind of sunscreen does he recommend for young children?
samples.target: Nonchemical sunscreens made only with titanium and zinc oxide.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, which kitchen appliances does he recommend owning?
samples.target: A centrifugal juicer, an orange juicer, and a food processor or high-quality blending machine.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, if a family includes animal products, roughly what maximum share of total calories does he suggest they make up?
samples.target: Perhaps 10 percent of total calories or less, rather than the 40 to 60 percent children eat today.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what share of the time does he say the family should be eating at home?
samples.target: 90 percent of the time.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how far does he say a pound of animal product should stretch for a family of five?
samples.target: It can be used for an entire family of five for a few days.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how many exposures does he cite research saying it takes for children to accept a new food, and after how many tries did most parents give up?
samples.target: It takes eight to fifteen times, yet about 75 percent of parents gave up after five tries.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what are the bananas, nuts, and carob quantities in the Fuhrman Fudgsicles recipe (serves 6-8)?
samples.target: 2 ripe bananas, 1 cup cashew nuts, and 2 tablespoons carob powder.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, in the Squash Fantasia recipe, what are the dried apricots and raisins soaked in, and for how long?
samples.target: In orange juice, overnight.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, what goes into the single-serving Blueberry and Flax Yogurt?
samples.target: 2 cups blueberries, 1/2 cup regular soy milk, 1 tablespoon ground flax seeds, and 3 medjool (or 6 Deglet Noor) dates, blended until smooth.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's book Disease-Proof Your Child, how long are the sweet potatoes baked for the Sweet Potato Pie with Secret Walnuts?
samples.target: 70 minutes, until soft.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of sleep, for how long at most does he say melatonin should be taken, and why?
samples.target: No more than about a week, because it suppresses the body's own melatonin production.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast, how long does he say halved artichokes should be steamed for the best flavor?
samples.target: Exactly 18 minutes (not 20), after cutting them in half and removing the choke.

samples.input: In Dr. Fuhrman's podcast discussion of plant milks, what are the only ingredients in the soy milk he uses?
samples.target: Two ingredients only: organic soybeans and purified water.
